fields.value: Visitors could approach and speak with Actroid-SIT using a microphone. fields.value: Induction rate was highest in the interruptible, parametric condition (62%, versus 48% and 38%); residence time was longest in that condition (52.5 s versus 33.3 s and 48.6 s). Residence-time differences between conditions 1 and 2, and 1 and 3, were significant at the 1% level; the authors attribute improved induction to the home-position idling motion and longer communication to interruptibility.

fields.value: The paper describes gaze motion planning alongside gesture adjustment for multiparty communication. It presents gaze as coordinated head and eye direction and as a way to look toward talkers or object locations.

quotes.text: we propose gesture adjustment suitable for human’s demand through parameterization and gaze motion planning which can communicate with multiple people and adjust a gesture to the location of talker and/or object.
Gaze angle Vx indicates degree between front direction and gaze direction as shown in Fig. 6.

fields.value: Gaze motion is used to look toward talkers and object points, including an idling motion that tracks a talker’s direction. The system also rapidly switches attention between people to support multiparty communication.

quotes.text: Therefore, this gesture performs as if idling motion by tracking talker’s direction.
This system can communicate with multiple people by rapid switching with each person, and adjustment gestures based on user or object location, and action for multi-person.

fields.value: The authors report that the home-position idling motion was associated with a higher induction rate, with the parametric and interruptible condition reaching over 60%. They report longer residence time with interruptible interaction and significant differences between the non-interruptible condition and both interruptible conditions.

quotes.text: We think that this improvement was thanks to idling motion by gesture 1 HOME POSITION. That is why Actroid is busy looking around people, and visitors feel easy to talk to Actroid.
Thus, we confirmed that interruptibility makes HRI more durable communication not only more reactive communication.

fields.value: The system uses a camera and microphone-color markers to detect talker location and count nearby people, speech recognition and keyphrase extraction, and an episode-rule selector. RMDB generates parameterized, interruptible body gestures; gaze direction is computed from head and eye angles with a sharing-rate model and convergence for object points. Components communicate through a Key-Value Store. The paper does not state that interaction was Wizard-of-Oz controlled.

quotes.text: We use a single camera which is IEEE 1394 camera (Sony DFW-VL500) and is located next to Actroid, for detecting talker’s position and counting the number of people around Actroid.
We assumed if someone has a microphone, he/she is a talker.

fields.value: The authors state that robot appearance and body gesture affect human impression, and that the android's human-like appearance is expected to help present multimodal information. They do not isolate or measure an embodiment effect in the experiment.

quotes.text: In HRI, an appearance of robot as well as its body gesture affects human impression.
Android robots are expected to be more effective for presenting multi-modal information because of their appearance unlike other robots.

fields.value: The paper presents an Actroid-SIT system for multiparty interaction that plans interruptible, parameterized gestures and gaze toward talkers or objects. In a field experiment, the interruptible and parametric condition had a 62% induction rate and the longest mean conversation residence time (52.5 seconds); the authors linked the induction result to the robot’s idling motion and longer interaction to interruptibility.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5; RQ6 — The paper describes gaze motion as head and eye direction and explains its role in tracking talkers, objects, and switching among people. It reports interaction outcomes and system implementation, identifies the Actroid-SIT embodiment, and discusses how appearance may affect impression, though it does not isolate embodiment effects.
